utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We assemble this morning for a Pre-Defence Conference, with a view to commencing the Defence case this afternoon at 2.15. The first matter that must be considered is whether there has now been, in sufficient compliance with Rule 65 ter, that is, an indication of the position of the Defence and its intentions with regard to evidence during the Defence case. There was a filed notification on the 16th of November, and, also, that dealt with a number of witnesses and also a list of exhibits. There has been no specific objection raised by the Prosecution and no request for any further information or particulars. That remains the position, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There had been an informal discussion with the Defence for further and better particulars in respect to some persons, and that was delivered to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very good. Well, it seems as though the Defence counsel have done a very good job; we thank you for that. It's something that will enable us to move on speedily. In due course, as we get into the defence, we will look at the length of the Defence case and the number of proposed witnesses. But for the moment, I think that can be allowed to remain while we start to get into the field of the Defence case. Now, the Defence Rule 65 notice indicated that there would be expert witnesses called. It seems, from that notice, that there has been not yet disclosed to the Prosecution any details of the evidence of those three expert witnesses. The Chamber needs to ensure that those reports are exchanged in good time to enable the case to proceed and to conclude readily. Could you indicate, Mr. Djordjevic, whether there is any plan that you have in mind as to the time when those reports will be available?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are waiting for two translations to be completed, that's one thing. Then we would need two weeks to finalise all these reports and file them. And I believe that will fit within the schedule of our work, as we are three weeks before a longer recess. But in any case, we need two weeks to provide the details concerning the evidence of these expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you're contemplating that those reports will be provided before we have the Christmas break, in December; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the intention of the Defence. Two weeks is the time we would like to request for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague, Mr. Djurdjic, who is more involved in that issue, says that by the end of this session we will be able to file two translations. Just after the recess, we would provide further details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you would like, then, to have a date fixed which was in the middle of January rather than December?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has in mind, Mr. Djordjevic, Monday, the 18th of January. Would that be convenient?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. I would also like to inform the Trial Chamber that it is the intention of the Defence that our expert witnesses give evidence at the end of our Defence case, that is, after all the other evidence. We want to put you on notice. But in any case, by 18th of January we would file all the necessary details for each of the expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 18th of January, 2010, will then be the date for the Defence to disclose the expert reports that it has in mind. There should be no problem then, should there, Mr. Stamp, for the Prosecution to be in a position to give notice under the Rules within the month that follows that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. We can work within that time-frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, we would propose to fix Monday, the 22nd of February, as the last day for the Prosecution's response under Rule 94 bis to the Defence notice. That would give you the 30 days and a couple more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now I notice, Mr. Djordjevic, that you are contemplating motions under Rule 92 ter for the evidence of a number of your proposed witnesses to be given in chief in written form. While that's indicated, as far as I know there's not yet been any motion. What is planned there by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence hopes that our motion will be filed within a month, that is, in January. It also depends on the time that will be available to us during the recess break. We believe that by the end of next month we will be able to file such a motion under 92 bis, ter, and possibly quater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The end of next month is the end of January --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ah, you're being cautious --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- December --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 30th, okay. So you're meaning the end of December?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] End of January, Your Honour. I am, in my mind, already in December. It would make no difference if it were the end of December because we would be in the middle of the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that you will have the last few days of -- in December because we will not sit for the whole of the last week, you will have that available, we would suggest Monday, the 4th of January, 2010, as the last day. That would seem to meet your needs?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully appreciate what you said, but I do have to draw your attention to the fact that in view of the holidays that we celebrate as Orthodox Christians, including our Christmas on the 7th of January, I would kindly ask you to put that dead-line after the 7th of January, otherwise we would not be able to fully comply. That's the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We were wanting you to have entirely free consciences by the time of your celebrations and have completed the work. The reason, obviously, is that you must file your motion, the Prosecution must have time to respond. We will then have to look at the motion, and you anticipate many witnesses, both 92 bis, ter, and quater. And it's not until the Chamber has decided that motion that it will be clear to you which witnesses will need to be here at what times, because the outcome of that motion will affect the times that your witnesses will need to give evidence. And if any are to give evidence under 92 bis, it will affect whether they need to be here at all, unless we specifically order cross-examination. So it would seem that the last day of the 4th of January, giving you plenty of time to be earlier if you wish, would be the most efficient to enable us to give you decisions before the end of January. I think if it's left later than that, it will affect the conduct of your case and the speed and efficiency with which we get through it. So perhaps you should work to yourselves getting the work done in 2009, that takes you to the end of 2009, and you can file the motions and then have a wonderful Christmas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honour. We accept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, what we would propose then is to formally order the 4th of January, in the expectation that you may file earlier, and then, Mr. Stamp, that you would respond by the 15th of January. They will be the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if we could have the normal 14-day period to respond. I think just at about that period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be flying from Jamaica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- quite a few of the team will be returning just then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean you would like until the 18th of January?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The 18th of January would be more convenient to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it will be a big day, the 18th of January, because that's when the Defence is filing its expert reports as well. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- yes, Mr. Stamp, you can have until the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I'm much obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we notice that there are 1.772 documents that you intend to offer as part of your case. First, how are you proceeding with translations of those documents? Will they be ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is like this: We have taken all the necessary steps to have all those documents that need to be translated translated in time. In other words, I expect that we will be able, in any case, to get all those documents that we have submitted translated in time so that they can be used in the course of our case. We are aware of this obligation, and in any case we expect that in a few weeks and in keeping with the schedule that we have proposed and in view of the order of witnesses, that we will have all the translations as required. That would be it in brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does this mean that you will be expecting to get translations as your case progresses?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will begin with our case obviously, and that's going to happen this afternoon. So my reply -- my answer would be yes. But if we are to discuss any -- to mention any dead-lines, let's say that would be by January 20th. I don't want -- I didn't want to say 18th because we didn't want all those things to happen on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if there is any difficulty with that very large number of documents and ensuring that you have finalised translations, it will be important to let the translation people know which documents you need at the early stages of your case so that they can give priority to the documents you will need with early witnesses. We don't want to find that they have translated the documents for your last witnesses but not the documents for the early witnesses. And there's also the question that once the translations are completed, the documents need to be uploaded into e-court, and that's a very large number of documents you have in mind. So it will be important that you and your team get on to the exhibits as early as possible, ensure that the original and the translation are available, and have them provided to those who have to upload them into the e-court system. Can we leave that with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. My legal assistant, Ms. O'Leary, has just told me that all of the documents that need to be translated have already been submitted and the translation unit has already been advised of the order that they need to be translated. But, in any case, we expect that all of those materials will be translated through the end of December. But out of an abundance of caution, we set the 20th January as the final dead-line when all of these documents and their translations will be already -- will have been uploaded in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And should we encounter any problems, we will do what we can do resolve them. As you know, it is possible that some documents might be tardy even if -- the translations of them -- even if we submit them all on time. But, in any case, we will keep you informed, and we will try to be on track. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will hope that the word "tardy" never arises in the course of the Defence case. Now, I think it's important for the Chamber to remind both parties of the procedural orders that will apply during the Defence case. What the Chamber has in mind is the same procedures that applied during the Prosecution case, only, of course, in reverse. To that end, if I could just remind everybody of the essential orders: The Defence is to disclose the witnesses that it intends to call two weeks before the commencement of the week in which a witness is to give evidence. In other words, we look at witnesses essentially week by week with two weeks' notice to the Prosecution and to the Chamber of the witnesses to be called in any week. That notice shall include an estimate of the time that the Defence anticipates will be needed, both for examination-in-chief and cross-examination; in other words, what the Chamber needs for its planning is to have an estimate of the length of time the witness will be here giving evidence. 48 hours before a witness is called to give evidence, the Defence shall give notice to the Prosecution and to the Registry Court Officer of the documents which the Defence intends to use with that witness. So 48 hours before a witness actually commences, both the Prosecution and the Registry Officer should know of the documents that it is intended to use by the Defence. The Prosecution shall give notice of its intention to use documents in cross-examination, first of all to the Registry Court Officer, 48 hours before the evidence of that witness commences; in other words, the same time as the Defence. All documents intended to be used with expert witnesses will be the subject of notice 48 hours in advance. In the case of the Prosecution, that will be 48 hours' notice to the Defence as well as the Court. For the Prosecution, all other documents will be subject of 24-hours' advance notice to the Defence. That is, 48-hours' notice to the Registry Court Officer for e-court purposes. And 24-hours' notice, minimum, to the Defence for all documents of ordinary witnesses. But in the case of expert witnesses, it's 48-hours' notice. Is that clear enough, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There seems to be one slight, and maybe I had it wrong, one slight difference between our obligations now and the Defence obligations when they were filing their notices. I'm wondering if the Court Officer needs 48 hours for the ordinary witnesses, or if the 24-hour notification could be sufficient for them. I say so because many times 48 hours before the witness is -- especially if they're moving quickly, we might not have the notices ready 48 hours before the ordinary crime based witness or a witness that we'd be going through quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 48 hours was the order when the Prosecution case --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Oh, I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- was proceeding --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and the point is the Registry has to identify the documents, get them all ready, so that when you call for them in the middle of cross-examination, they can be brought up instantly. If you're down to 24 hours, with quite a number of documents happening in your case and documents of some number being required in other cases, we can find that there has not been sufficient time allowed for the uploading into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So 48 hours it really needs to be, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware now of three pending motions which it is dealing with. This is the Prosecution's motion to re-open the case to admit exhibits from the bar table. The Defence has filed its response to that motion, and a decision can be expected, I would think, in the course of this week. The second motion is the Prosecution's motion to submit proof of death charts that was filed on the 23rd of November. The Defence is yet to respond. Its time for doing so will finish on the 7th of December. There was received this morning a Defence motion to add documents to the Rule 65 ter list. There has been no time, of course, for the Prosecution to consider that. The Chamber would observe that it would be helpful if it is able to respond to that in a much shorter time than usual because it is useful for planning of witnesses to know whether documents are to be available or not. My quick look at the motion suggested that it would not be very difficult for the Prosecution to respond in an earlier time. We will not make a formal order in case there really is a difficulty we have not foreseen, but we do encourage the Prosecution to look, as soon as possible, at that new motion. Is there any other matter that you feel you need to raise, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Regarding next witnesses, we would seek the Chamber's guidance as to what to file about notice today for the week of 14th December. Given the large amount of time, we have noticed for this witnesses if we assume the same amount of time for cross and factor in some time for Chambers' questions, we see Mr. Djordjevic being on the stand for these two weeks' time. We have noticed one more witness for the second week, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not sure your client was terribly overjoyed to hear that, but we understand the estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The facts is talking. So we have noticed one more witness for the second week, but we're not certain how many we should be making arrangements for in this time, seeing as we don't want to have people to travel unnecessarily. Therefore, we'd ask the Trial Chamber to provide guidance as to how many witnesses it thinks would be appropriate to notice today or if any more are required at all for notice before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. You may recall, Mr. Djordjevic, that we did indicate that we would only sit at the beginning of that last week and not through the whole week. I think the best guidance we can give - we're conscious of the problems of bringing witnesses, the time, and the cost - and what we would suggest is that you should plan to fill Monday, the 14th of December, but not plan for new witnesses after the Monday. If the witness called for Monday, the 14th, doesn't finish that day, we will continue to sit to finish that witness. But don't plan for additional witnesses beyond Monday, the 14th. Now, of course, a lot will depend on precisely how long it proves to be that your client will give evidence. It -- it's just possible that he will be giving evidence on Monday, the 14th, still. We're aware of that. But if it looks as though he will finish during the preceding week, we'll then have one or two witnesses - as you judge - to finish by the end of Monday, the 14th of December. If your judgement is in error and the witness continues beyond that, the Chamber will hear the end of that witness. But don't try to bring fresh witnesses after that. Avoid the cost and the time involved in doing that. Is that guidance enough for your purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That's what I thought. Thank you for that. Now I would like to raise another issue. We are not certain how the Trial Chamber was planning to proceed, but the Defence would request that the testimony of Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic begin tomorrow morning instead of today, immediately following opening statements. There are several reasons for this. As you are well aware, there are many documents noticed on both sides for the witness. The Defence sent a list on Tuesday evening, but it seems there was a court holiday on Friday. The Defence received the cross-examine document list only yesterday afternoon. This does not allow us ample time to review nor does it offer him the same conditions as afforded other witnesses here who were allowed to know the documents the other party would use in advance of testimony. As we cannot have full access to our client the way a party does with its other witnesses who are not in custody, we would ask that the conditions for him testifying be at least similar to those who have testified against him. Further, while we have taken a large amount of time to meet with our client that still remains, that once he begins testimony he will be uncounseled for an indefinite amount of time, possibly two weeks. Because today is a Monday, and we were not allowed to visit over the weekend as a counsel, we would like it if you permit him to start tomorrow, as I said, to meet him in the jail, in the custody, from 6.00 to 8.00 p.m., to make sure all last matters are in order, including next witnesses who may come after him this month. Additionally, today is an afternoon sitting on a long day, going into the morning sitting. This is a tiring combination for all of us, but we hate to put that strain on our client right away, considering that he may be testifying for much longer than any other witnesses in this trial. At the beginning of this trial, the Prosecution started their first witness the day following opening. Arguments which were held on an additionally separate day from the Pre-Trial Conference. As Mr. Djordjevic is present and involved in all, it is asking a lot of him to start the same day as the Pre-Defence Conference and opening statement. In requesting this, we assure Your Honours that this will have no significant bearing on the time and will actually serve to help everything be more organised and run more smoothly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm inclined to object to the application. The Prosecution had put a lot of effort in getting along today, but I see the reasons given by counsel. One of them I don't think has much merit, but there may be something to consider in the others. So I will leave that one in the hands of the Chamber, but just to indicate that we are ready to proceed this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djordjevic, your eloquence has been to noticeable effect. The Chamber agrees that your client should commence his evidence tomorrow at 9.00. We will sit at 2.15 this afternoon to hear the opening address of counsel and then adjourn to resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your understanding, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any matter that you wish to raise at this stage, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think counsel alluded to it just now when he indicated what their position is in respect to their consulting with the accused once he has proceeded to testify. And I would ask the Court if the Court could give us and give the Defence some guidance, just for the record, as to the type and nature of contact they should have with him once his testimony proceeds. Although, I believe counsel has already indicated that it is limited, but I think for the record we should know where we stand on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Stamp. I understood from the submissions of Mr. Djordjevic that the position was correctly and fully understood by the Defence. But just so that it is clear, in the absence of any specific order by the Chamber, there would be no contact between counsel and the accused during the course of his evidence. So once he commences evidence tomorrow morning, counsel will not speak to him until he has completed all stages of his evidence. If there is some particular difficulty or emergency, that must be raised with the Chamber for some specific direction. In the absence of that, what I've indicated is the normal position which will apply. And I'm sure that's what Mr. Djordjevic had in mind from what he said. If there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And lastly, Your Honour, I think since we're all here I should just state that in respect to the motion to amend the 65 ter list we have no objections to the request to amend the list, without making any comments on the merits of the documents. But insofar as it seeks to amend the Defence 65 ter list to add 15, I think, proposed exhibits, we do not object to that motion. We had seen the motion, a courtesy copy, earlier this morning, and there were some issues in respect to one of the documents. But I think we are in a position to resolve that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. And in light of that, the Chamber would indicate now that, in the absence of any objection, it will grant the motion. So the Rule 65 ter list of the Defence is now amended to add the documents proposed in the motion. There will be no further written order by the Chamber. Everything is complete. You can proceed on that basis, Mr. Djordjevic. That being the case, we seem to have dealt with all matters that need to be dealt with now. We will adjourn until 2.15 to commence the opening statement. Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of November, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.18 a.m.,
